# Finite witness / Radon / cap-cover investigation

This file records rigorous lemmas and an obstruction to a weakened functional relaxation. It does not contain a proof of Oertel's conjecture.

## 1. What an ordinary mixed Helly certificate supplies

Let `μ` be mixed-integer volume normalized to total mass one. If the depth region at threshold `α` misses `Z^n×R^d`, the mixed Helly theorem supplies at most `2^n(d+1)` halfspaces whose relevant intersection already misses that set. Their complementary small caps cover `S`, so the union bound gives the familiar `1/[2^n(d+1)]` constant. The union-bound argument contains no mechanism that yields `γ_d`.

The following proposed repair is false: improve each group of at most `d+1` balanced caps individually by the continuous Grünbaum factor. For example, take `n=d=2`, integer support equal to the vertices of a unimodular triangle, and equal small disks as the continuous fibers. Put their continuous centers at the vertices of an equilateral triangle. Three closed halfplanes through the continuous origin, with outward normals toward those vertices, cover the entire continuous plane and each capture exactly one fiber. Every cap has one third of the mass, below `γ_2=4/9`. The actual set is induced by the convex hull of the three fibers: its projection is a unimodular triangle, so it has no further integer fibers. A successful certificate must preserve a common lattice budget across all cap groups.

## 2. A rigorous small-support lemma

Suppose there are `N` positive-volume integer fibers. If `N≤2^n`, the required inequality follows immediately. Choose a fiber of maximal volume, and choose its ordinary centroid. Every ambient halfspace containing this point either contains the whole selected fiber (if its continuous normal vanishes) or intersects that fiber in a continuous halfspace containing its centroid. In the latter case, continuous Grünbaum gives a cap of at least `γ_d` times that fiber's volume. The selected fiber has at least `1/N≥2^-n` of the total volume.

Consequently, a full-volume counterexample would have more than `2^n` positive fibers. Two of their indices have the same parity, and their integer midpoint has a positive-volume fiber containing their Minkowski average.

This observation alone does not justify a compression or induction. Deleting either endpoint changes both the body and the denominator, while enlarging the midpoint may increase the denominator and move all candidate depth optima. No monotonicity for that operation has been proved here.

## 3. Exact midpoint compatibility

For `u,v∈Z^n` with integer midpoint `m=(u+v)/2`, convexity gives

`(K_u+K_v)/2 ⊂ K_m`.

Hence, for nonempty full-dimensional endpoint fibers, Brunn–Minkowski gives

`vol(K_m)^(1/d) ≥ [vol(K_u)^(1/d)+vol(K_v)^(1/d)]/2`.

For a fixed ambient halfspace `H`, its fiberwise sections satisfy the stronger set-valued relation

`[(K_u∩H_u)+(K_v∩H_v)]/2 ⊂ K_m∩H_m`.

The same holds for the complementary open halfspace. Brunn–Minkowski can be applied when both endpoint sections are nonempty. A zero-volume empty section cannot be treated as an ordinary body of volume zero in this argument: Minkowski addition with an empty set is empty, and interpolation to a positive endpoint then need not give a lower bound at intermediate indices.

## 4. Scalar cap concavity does not encode sufficient compatibility

Consider the following relaxation for `n=1,d=2`, with indices `z=0,1,2,3,4`:

`w(z)=1`, and `v_i(z)=1` if `z=i`, `v_i(z)=0` otherwise, for `i=0,…,4`.

The root `w^(1/d)` is concave. Every cap root `v_i^(1/d)` is concave on its convex positive support, a singleton. Every index is covered, since `Σ_i v_i(z)=w(z)`. Each total cap mass is one fifth of the total mass, strictly smaller than `2/9`.

Even requiring a continuous concave-root extension on a nondegenerate positive-support interval does not fix this: use

`v_i(t) = max(1−10|t−i|,0)^d`

on the projection interval `[0,4]`. Its positive support is an interval, and its `1/d` power is concave there; the integer samples remain as above.

These data cannot arise simultaneously from the indicated caps of a common convex body. They demonstrate that separate Brunn–Minkowski concavity statements for the total fiber volumes and individual cap volumes lose essential common-body information. Thus a finite-witness proof cannot replace all fiber sets by those scalar profiles without an additional proved compatibility theorem.

## 5. Why constant-volume fibers expose that relaxation's defect

For `n=1`, suppose the positive integer fibers are `K_0,…,K_m`, with equal volume `V>0`, and `m≥2`. For three consecutive fibers, midpoint inclusion and Brunn–Minkowski give

`V ≥ vol((K_i+K_{i+2})/2) ≥ V`.

Equality in Brunn–Minkowski implies that the endpoint fibers are homothetic; equal volumes make them translates. Equality of volume in the full-dimensional convex inclusion makes the middle fiber their exact Minkowski average. Applying this to every consecutive triple yields a common convex body `K` and vectors `b,a` such that `K_i=K+b+i a` for every integer `i`.

Here equality of two full-dimensional compact convex bodies under inclusion follows directly: strict inclusion supplies a point outside the smaller body, and taking its convex hull with an interior ball of the smaller body produces positive volume outside the smaller body.

The constant-volume family therefore becomes a product after the lattice-preserving shear `(z,x)↦(z,x−b−za)`. For any median integer index and the centroid of `K`, at least half the fiber centroids lie in each ambient halfspace containing that point. Applying continuous Grünbaum in each of those fibers proves `γ_d/2`. The cases of one or two fibers follow from the small-support lemma.

This is an exact restricted theorem, not an extension to unequal fiber volumes. A quantitative form of the midpoint equality mechanism could be relevant, but no suitable inequality with the required sharp global constants has been established here.

## 6. A valid affine-centroid theorem

More generally, assume the fiber centroid map is affine on its integer support: `c_z=A z+b`. Give each index the weight `vol(K_z)`. A weighted Doignon centerpoint supplies an integer support point `z_*` having projection depth at least `2^-n`. Choose `y=(z_*,c_{z_*})`.

For an ambient halfspace `a·z+v·x≥t` containing `y`, the condition that a fiber centroid belong to the halfspace is

`(a+A^T v)·z≥t−v·b`.

If its normal vanishes, all fiber centroids belong to the halfspace; otherwise this is a projection halfspace containing `z_*`. Those indices carry at least `2^-n` of the total weight. On each corresponding fiber the cap has at least `γ_d` of the fiber volume. Summing proves the desired product constant under this affine-centroid hypothesis.

The hypothesis is substantive. Even the convex planar body `{(s,t):−2≤s≤2, s²≤t≤5}` has nonaffine centroid graph `t=(s²+5)/2`. The separate exact certificate in `candidate a3a3b42ddbc25ef5` also rules out repairing the issue by using only integer-coordinate exponential tilts.

## Route status

The ordinary finite Helly certificate remains insufficient. Its needed improvement is a theorem about simultaneous convex interpolation of the actual fibers and cap cuts; separate cap concavity and independent improvement of cap groups both fail. No compression, Radon, Tverberg, or witness-volume monotonicity giving the sharp constant has been proved in this route.
